rationale: Question 6464ac4e45e546e99aff4d88c0a145c8-question-0 needs a discriminating observation: the single retained sighting of a demoted peer still reporting itself as a voter, against native reruns in which nothing lagged. This experiment samples every node's own configuration view (GetConfiguration, the atomic copy written by setLatestConfiguration) together with its LastIndex every 20ms across a DemoteVoter call and for ten seconds afterwards, in the same per-node timing as the extended-window scenario, three times. Each node's event distinguishes the two competing explanations by construction: a view that stays old while that node's LastIndex never reaches the configuration entry's index is a delivery stall, while a view that stays old after the node's log already contains that index would point at configuration-entry processing instead.

scope.description: Follow one committed voter-to-non-voter transition in a healthy 4-node cluster while sampling every node's own configuration view and log index, three independent runs.
assumptions: Real target constructors and APIs only: BootstrapCluster, NewRaft, DemoteVoter, GetConfiguration, LastIndex; per-node Config values (leader 20s, near 6s, far voters 3s), all ValidateConfig-clean.

Only the leader is bootstrapped; the other three start with empty configurations and adopt them through normal replication, so the cluster is the same construction as the extended-window experiment that produced the unexplained sighting.
Before the transition the harness waits until every follower reports itself with a vote and has LastIndex >= 2, so the baseline is uniform and the transition is the only event under observation.
Sampling is every 20ms for ten seconds after the transition is committed on the leader; a node counts as converged at the first sample where its own view shows the demoted peer without a vote.
Three runs in one execution; the transports stay fully connected and healthy throughout, so any lag observed is not caused by a partition.
excluded: No partition, no snapshots, no restarts or crash-recovery, and no client traffic besides the configuration change itself.
The configuration index used for the consistency check is read from the leader after the change returns; the harness does not inspect the follower's log store directly.

experiment.prefix: Four nodes are created (identity = in-memory transport address), wired fully connected and started; only the first is bootstrapped with the four-voter configuration, so it is the deterministic first leader and the others adopt the configuration through replication. The harness waits for that leader, then waits until every follower reports itself with a vote and has LastIndex >= 2, and emits a baseline CA_EVENT with each node's view of the near node and its LastIndex. It then calls DemoteVoter(near, prevIndex 0, timeout 10s), waits for the future (which returns when the entry is committed on the leader), records the leader's LastIndex as the configuration index, and polls every node every 20ms for ten seconds: each poll reads that node's GetConfiguration view of the near node's suffrage and its LastIndex. A node counts as converged at the first poll where its view shows the near node without a vote; the harness also keeps the highest LastIndex seen while that node's view was still old. One demotion_view CA_EVENT is emitted per node with converged, converged_ms, stale_observed, stale_max_last_index, the configuration index, index_passed_while_stale, and the node's end state and LastIndex.
experiment.responsibility: Configuration propagation from the leader's committed membership change to each peer's own view of its suffrage, as consumed by that peer's election eligibility (runFollower checks hasVote on its latest configuration before campaigning) and by quorum arithmetic on the leader.

comparisons.description: Run 1: every node (including the demoted one) reports the new suffrage within the ten second observation window on a healthy transport; a node that never converges is contradicted here.
Run 1 consistency: no node's view may still be old at a sample where that node's own LastIndex already reached the configuration entry, which would separate a processing gap from a delivery lag.
